svg.title: Россия на карте
svg.desc: Cover map for Глава 1. A simplified map of European Russia with the seas in pale blue-grey: the Baltic and the Gulf of Finland at Petersburg, the White and Barents seas to the north, the Black Sea and the Caspian to the south. A dashed line along the Urals and the Ural river divides Европа (left) from Азия (right); Россия is written large across the country. The Volga runs from the north-west past the Yaroslavl region, east to Kazan and south to the Caspian; the Oka flows from the west past Рязань and joins the Volga. Петербург is in the north-west, Москва in the centre, away from the Volga. A black-and-white railway runs from Moscow south-east through Ryazan to a small district town. A box around Ryazan is enlarged in an inset at bottom right, Рязанская губерния: the Oka and Рязань, the railway (железная дорога) to the уездный город inside a dashed уезд outline, and a dotted road (дорога) past a field and a wood to the village Берёзовка, a small red dot on a little river. Berezovka is too small to appear on the large map.
